title: Privacy you can verify
lead: We are not asking you to take our word for it. The encryption scheme is described below, and its implementation lives in a public repository — read the code and check it yourself.
encryptedLead: Nothing reaches the database in plain form: every piece of user data we store is encrypted, not just a hand-picked set of fields.
loggingDesc: In production the services never write user data to the logs — not even for debugging.
loggingYes: Events and technical errors: service start and stop, response codes, timeouts, connection failures. That is exactly what air_logger handles.
loggingNo: Conversation content, message bodies and call transcripts, customer contacts, API keys and tokens.
eraseDesc: The decision is yours and yours alone. You can wipe everything from your dashboard at any time — after that nothing of yours is left in the database.

erase.dialogs: Conversations and the entire message history

eraseNote: Erasure is irreversible: the data cannot be restored afterwards — not even by us.

step1.title: MasterKey password
step1.desc: You choose it yourself. We never store it in plain form and cannot look it up.

step2.title: KDF · key derivation
step2.desc: The encryption key is derived from the password deterministically. The password cannot be reconstructed back from it.

step3.title: AES-GCM
step3.desc: Symmetric encryption with integrity protection: tampered data will not silently decrypt.

step4.title: Storage
step4.desc: Only ciphertext reaches the database. Without your key it is just a blob of bytes.

verifyTitle: Trust that is verifiable, not declared
verifyDesc: Open source is not marketing here, it is a control mechanism: there is simply nowhere to hide data access or a hidden markup inside a repository anyone can read.
note: The flip side of an honest scheme: if you forget your MasterKey password, access to the encrypted data is lost. Neither we nor anyone else can restore it.
diagramAlt: Encryption scheme: MasterKey password, key derivation, AES-GCM encryption and ciphertext stored in the database
